title: Physics: Foundations to Frontiers
description: A curated physics knowledge graph: Newtonian, Lagrangian, and Hamiltonian mechanics through quantum field theory, AdS/CFT, the black-hole information problem, and today's quantum-gravity frontiers. Includes condensed matter and nonequilibrium statistical physics, plus cross-domain bridges into economics (econophysics) and music (symmetry and counterpoint). Full English notes on every concept.

title: Mathematics: Foundations to Langlands
description: A curated mathematics knowledge graph: set theory, analysis, algebra, geometry, probability, and complexity, extended to algebraic geometry, the Langlands program, number theory, and combinatorics. Rich bridge notes connect functional analysis to quantum mechanics, modular forms to string theory, and mathematics to economics and art. Full English notes on every concept.

title: Economics: Micro to Econometrics
description: A curated economics knowledge graph: micro and macro foundations, game theory, behavioral and neuroeconomics, economic history, crises, financial engineering, and modern econometrics (causal inference, IV/DID/RDD). Bridged to statistical mechanics and probability for a genuinely cross-domain view. Full English notes on every concept.

title: Art: Aesthetics, Traditions, and Artists
description: A curated art knowledge graph: aesthetics and philosophy of art, neuroaesthetics, music, visual art and literature foundations, non-western total-art traditions (Natya Shastra, noh, jingju), and 13 artist profiles from Bach and Hokusai to Frida Kahlo and Zaha Hadid, linked by influence ties. Full English notes on every concept.

title: Default Agents
description: Two agents and four skills every space starts with. The Maker does the work in one loop and the Checker verifies it without the Maker's context; the know-how lives in skill nodes: keep the graph honest, research from measurement, curate documents, review claims. Add a skill, not an agent, when your space needs more. Fill reads, gates and paths with your own.

title: Software Agents
description: Five roles for a code repository, with the handoffs between them as edges: a developer (one change, one branch, one pull request, one episode), a gate runner (runs the gates, never edits), a checklist reviewer (ticks the plan against the diff), a judgement reviewer (adversarial read for correctness and over-engineering) and a security auditor (findings become packages, never fixes in place). Roles only: add your own reads, gates and paths.

title: Design Agents
description: Three roles for a design system: a designer who keeps token values on graph nodes and the reasons in decisions, pulling the token file and syncing consumers in the same session; a design reviewer who measures contrast and drift and never edits; and a design researcher who turns interviews into records attached to the concepts they are about. Roles only: add your own reads, gates and paths.

title: Infra and Ops Agents
description: Three roles for the deploy plane: an infrastructure role that writes the declaration and stops at plan (a person applies), an operations role that diagnoses deploys and incidents from the logs and never changes state, and a release role that prepares the bump, changelog and tag readiness a person publishes. Roles only: add your own reads, gates and paths.

title: Copy and Marketing Agents
description: Three roles for product copy and claims: a copy writer who drafts lines for review and never commits, a copy owner who keeps inventory and parity between languages and ships only lines read aloud, and a marketing role that ties every capability claim to the build it is true on and never prices or sends. Roles only: add your own reads, gates and paths.
